subject: SE and Confidence intervals in occupancy models

messages.author: fdaa54d30ab7b913
messages.subject: SE and Confidence intervals in occupancy models
parts:
Dear list members,

I have an occuoancy model fitted with unmarked with these estimates:


> pre
  Predicted          SE        lower     upper    amb
1 0.4603569 0.214784272 1.354700e-01 0.8228277 arroyo
2 0.9999035 0.004630678 1.442191e-37 1.0000000 laguna
3 0.3683033 0.175737047 1.171227e-01 0.7192934  mixto

I don´t understand why the estiamte with the lower standard error has the wider confidence interval.

Any insight will be appreciated.

Manuel

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Re: SE and Confidence intervals in occupancy models
parts:
Manuel,
If you notice this same issue on the regression coefficients in your model, you can try calculating profile likelihood intervals rather than normal confidence intervals on those coefficients [use: method="profile" within confint() ].  

As far as I can tell, you can't calculate profile likelihood intervals on predictions using existing unmarked infrastructure (but someone please chime in if I am incorrect here), but you could potentially do it by hand if you wanted to.  :O)
